calib_weights / calib_weights_fit: integrated precision-weight storage (0.6.0)

Source: calib_weights_SPEC.md

Goal. Store precision weights from more than one weighting model in the existing two tables, so users download one bundle with one set of weights, and add the fields the additive measurement-error model needs. Nothing about the sample hierarchy changes.

Ownership. The schema is defined here (R/calib_schema.sql, mirrored by weights_contract()); curveRweights produces the values; the i-spi-compute worker writes them; I-SPI reads them. A test keeps the DDL and weights_contract() in sync.

Decisions

  1. Keys unchanged. calib_weights: (curve_id, method, sampleid, patientid, timeperiod, dilution), the same sample hierarchy as calib_samples. calib_weights_fit: (multiplate_group_id, method).
  2. One weight set per (sample, method). model is an ordinary column, not part of the key. Re-running with another model replaces the set (the workers already delete by key then insert). A side-by-side store can be added later by adding model to the keys without disturbing readers.
  3. sigma, w, w_norm mean the same in every model: total SD, inverse-variance weight, mean-1 weight under the fitted model. Consumers of those columns are model-agnostic.
  4. New columns are nullable, NULL = does not apply to the model that wrote the row, except model (NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘multiplicative’: what every pre-0.6.0 row used). Pre-0.6.0 rows therefore remain valid and unchanged.
  5. No CHECK on model (family convention); validate_weights_table() enforces it before writing. censor_type carries the same CHECK as calib_samples.
  6. Not added: a foreign key from calib_weights to calib_samples. It would guarantee identical samples but cascade-delete weights when a curve is recalibrated, a behaviour change; decide separately.

Added columns (0.6.0)

calib_weights: model, weights_pkg_version, v_meas, tau2, reliability, reliability_lo, reliability_hi, censor_type, bound. calib_weights_fit: model, weights_pkg_version, tau, tau_lo, tau_hi, kappa, kappa_lo, kappa_hi, reliability, reliability_lo, reliability_hi, fix_beta1, n_censored, identifiability. Per-column meaning: weights_contract().

Row semantics

  • multiplicative: sigma = phi * se^beta1. Fills phi, beta1 (+ intervals). tau, kappa, reliability, v_meas, tau2, censor_type, bound stay NULL.
  • additive: sigma^2 = tau2 + v_meas, v_meas = kappa^2 * se^(2 beta1). Fills tau, kappa, reliability, fix_beta1, n_censored, identifiability; beta1 = 1 when fixed (CI NULL); phi, phi_lo, phi_hi NULL. Censored samples keep their row: censor_type and bound set, w_norm NULL (represented by the bound, not a weight).

Applying

R/calib_schema.sql is idempotent. On the live DB the CREATEs skip and the ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS blocks add the columns; on a fresh DB the result has the identical column order (verified on a scratch PostgreSQL 16: upgraded vs fresh layouts identical; second apply a no-op). i-spi-compute migration 010 is the same two ALTER statements.
